messages.content: I need to be in Minneapolis for an operations review on Thursday, May 14. The office is downtown, and I have to be there by 9:30 a.m. The review ends at 4:00. Compare flying from Chicago that morning with going Wednesday evening.
I can compare both schedules using realistic transfer time from MSP. Which Chicago airport should I use, and where downtown is the office?
Use O'Hare. The office is near Nicollet Mall and South 8th Street.

For a 9:30 arrival, I would plan on 25 to 35 minutes from MSP to the office by taxi or rideshare, plus roughly 20 minutes to get off the aircraft and reach the pickup area. That makes an arrival at MSP by about 8:20 a.m. the practical limit, with earlier being safer.

The strongest same-day option currently departs ORD at 6:00 a.m. and arrives MSP at 7:32 a.m., nonstop. The return departs MSP at 6:20 p.m. and reaches ORD at 7:52 p.m. The round trip is $397 in standard economy.
Walk me through the morning. Is that actually enough time, or does it only work if everything is perfect?

With an on-time 7:32 arrival, a reasonable timeline is:

7:32 a.m. touchdown
7:45-7:55 a.m. off the aircraft and heading to ground transportation
8:00-8:10 a.m. in a taxi or rideshare
8:30-8:45 a.m. at the office

That leaves about 45 to 60 minutes before the review. It does not require a perfect transfer, but a delay of roughly 45 minutes would consume most of the buffer. A cancellation or longer delay would leave no workable backup that morning.
What is the next-best same-day flight?

A second nonstop leaves ORD at 6:15 a.m. and arrives at 7:46 a.m. Its return leaves MSP at 7:10 p.m. and arrives at ORD at 8:43 p.m. The fare is $366.

It saves $31, but the later arrival reduces the downtown buffer by 14 minutes. I would keep the 6:00 a.m. itinerary as the stronger same-day plan.
Now compare Wednesday evening. I don't need to arrive especially early, but I don't want this turning into half a day away from work.

The best compact evening-before itinerary leaves ORD Wednesday at 6:30 p.m. and arrives MSP at 8:03 p.m., nonstop. Returning Thursday, the 6:20 p.m. flight reaches ORD at 7:52 p.m. Airfare is $344.

Allowing for the trip from MSP, you would likely reach a downtown hotel around 9:00 p.m. Thursday morning would then be a short walk or local ride to the office. Compared with the same-day plan, it adds one hotel night and Wednesday evening away, but removes the operational risk around the 9:30 start.
Is there a later Wednesday flight that still gets me downtown at a reasonable hour?

There is a nonstop at 7:10 p.m., arriving MSP at 8:42 p.m. You would probably reach a downtown hotel between 9:35 and 10:00 p.m. Paired with the same 6:20 p.m. return, the fare is $329.

A later option arrives after 10:00 p.m., which would put hotel arrival near 11:00 and offers little benefit beyond another hour in Chicago.
Keep the 6:00 a.m. same-day flight as the main option. For Wednesday, use the 7:10 p.m. departure since that still seems manageable. Does the 6:20 return give me enough time after a 4:00 finish?

Yes, provided the review ends close to schedule. Leaving the Nicollet Mall area around 4:10 p.m. should put you at MSP around 4:40 to 4:55. That leaves approximately 85 to 100 minutes before the 6:20 departure. Even with traffic pushing the ride to 45 minutes, you should still arrive about an hour before departure.

I would not use an earlier return. The next flight after 6:20 is the 7:10 p.m. option, which can serve as a fallback comparison but is not necessary for the planned schedule.
Good. Don't book either yet. Next I want to see whether the hotel cost makes the evening flight worth it.

Nothing has been booked. I’ll carry forward these two plans for the lodging and total-cost comparison:

Same day: Thursday, May 14, nonstop ORD-MSP from 6:00 to 7:32 a.m.; nonstop MSP-ORD from 6:20 to 7:52 p.m.; $397 round trip.

Evening before: Wednesday, May 13, nonstop ORD-MSP from 7:10 to 8:42 p.m.; the same Thursday return from 6:20 to 7:52 p.m.; $329 round trip, plus one downtown hotel night and the related ground transportation.
